overall: The AG resolved both complaints by informal action and found no Open Meeting Law violation. Email between one member and the Town Administrator did not reach a quorum; the records issue belongs under the Public Records Law; the secret-ballot claim was raised too late to review.

allegations.summary: A Committee member allegedly expressed opinions on a Committee matter in an email to the Town Administrator, which the complainant said violated the OML.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, communications between one member and the Town Administrator that do not otherwise reach a quorum of the Committee, even where an opinion is expressed, would not constitute deliberation.

allegations.summary: The Committee allegedly failed to produce audio recordings of its meetings in response to a February 23 public records request.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Open Meeting Law does not govern a public body's obligation to respond to requests for audio recording, which fall under the Public Records Law, G.L. c. 66, § 10.

allegations.summary: On appeal, the complainant alleged the Committee voted by secret ballot; this was not in the original complaint to the Committee, so it was not reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: Because these allegations were not part of the original complaint, we do not review them now.
